newsitem.title: UK: North Sea wet market active, prompt spreads firmer.
newsitem.headline: North Sea wet market active, prompt spreads firmer.

text.p: North Sea physical markets saw active trade on a couple of sweet grades on Tuesday with differentials edging up a few cents, traders said.

Ekofisk saw between two and four cargoes move over the day. The two deals which were confirmed were at Dated Brent +15 and +16 cents. Regular Ekofisk buyers said they saw no further July Ekofisks for sale. Two Oseberg cargoes traded, one confirmed at Dated Brent +20 cents.

No Brent trade was reported and the market remained at August +5/+15 cents with sellers holding out for one buyer who is thought to need a further three cargoes to fill a last decade July VLCC loader destined for the U.S.
The single Brent cargo in today's paper chains was kept before the five o'clock deadline by traders Aron.
On the paper market action concentrated on the Aug/Sept which moved up to six times between -11 and -9 cents. Late talk put the spread at -10/-9 cents and the Sep/Oct -15/-13 cents.
The only CFD reported was a July 14-25 at a strong Sept -22 cents. Late talk put next weeks (July 14-18) at Sept -24/-20 cents with the July 21-25 week at Sept -27/-23 cents.
Traders said availabilities were tight but said that field maintenance in August which will result in reduced North Sea output was already factored into the market.
"Everyone is aware of what August will bring but the whole thing depends on Iraq - totally on Iraq," one said.
"We know Iraqi crude will come onto the market in August but the question of when in August and how much are still to be answered," another added.
A U.N. official said on Tuesday they hope to receive the Iraqi food distribution plan by 2000 GMT.
